chunks: So I swear by the evening twilight,

key_terms.الشَّفَقِ: The red glow of the sky at sunset or sunrise, used here as an oath by God.

ai.seo_question: What does the oath by 'al-shafaq' (twilight) signify in Surah Al-Inshiqaq?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the oath by the *shafaq* (the red glow after sunset) highlights the transient nature of worldly signs compared to the eternal reality of the Hereafter, reinforcing the concept of *Qiyamah* (Resurrection). This verse sets the stage for the cosmic upheaval described in the surah, which Shia scholars often link to the spiritual awakening of the faithful and the ultimate justice of Imam al-Mahdi (aj). The emphasis on divine power serves as a reminder that just as the sky will be split, the barriers between the seen and unseen worlds will dissolve for accountability.
